title: Broomstick lace triangular shawl
excerpt: A triangular shawl worked in fingering yarn using broomstick lace clusters. Increases at the centre spine grow the shawl from the top down to a deep, draping point.
sourceNotes: A top-down triangular shawl in broomstick lace with a central spine increase. Each lace row adds width at both sides and at the centre.

glossaryTerms.definition: An increase worked at the centre of a shawl row to create the ridge that divides the two halves and adds the triangular shaping.
The unit of broomstick lace formed by slipping a group of enlarged loops off the dowel and working double crochets through their shared base.

crochet.gaugeText: 3 clusters (15 sts) x 6 rows = 10 cm in broomstick lace on 3.5 mm hook.
crochet.finishedSizeText: Approx. 140 cm wingspan x 65 cm deep at centre.

content.text: This shawl grows from a 3-stitch cast-on at the top edge. A
at the centre of each cluster row, together with edge increases, add 5 stitches every repeat. The
are worked in groups of 5 loops.
Chain 3. Row 1: dc in 2nd ch, ch 1 (spine), dc in last ch (3 sts). Do not turn.

Loop row: draw up a loop from every stitch and the spine chain onto the dowel. Add 1 extra loop at each end and 2 at the spine chain for increases. Cluster row: work clusters of 5 from the left half, work 2 dc in the spine loop (spine increase), then continue clusters across the right half. Repeat loop and cluster rows, always adding the spine and edge increases, until the wingspan reaches 140 cm.
Fasten off and weave in the ends with the tapestry needle. Block to shape by pinning the tip down and the wings out.
